title: DirectionLight3D under SDFGI has a serious light leakage problem
body: ### Tested versions Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9174) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700KF (24 threads) - 63.82 GiB memory ### System information Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9174) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700KF (24 threads) - 63.82 GiB memory ### Issue description When I was testing the 3D capabilities of Godot 4.6, I found that when SDFGI is enabled, DirectLight3D directly penetrates non-closed walls and affects objects inside completely enclosed spaces. ### Steps to reproduce ## Test 1 The test scenario specifications are as follows: 1. Indoor, enclosed space 2. Environment background set to CustomColor black, only SDFGI enabled, all parameters default. 3. Enclose the space by joining 0.5m thick CSGBoxes in six directions. 4. Add a DirectLight3D, enable shadows, and illuminate from one side. My expected result is that the room should be completely dark, but the result is unexpected. In a completely enclosed room, all materials with reflective properties in the room emit light. I once suspected that it might be related to the ambient light. I set the ambient light of the Environment to red, but the color of these lights did not change. I went to modify the indirect energy parameter of DirectLight3D and found that the light emitted by these objects is affected. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e74a65a-f1f4-4b40-b39a-f12abd88e61f ## Test 2 - Attempt to find a way to completely block DirectionLight3D I want to know if DirectLight3D cannot block indirect energy when SDFGI is enabled. So, I placed another 10m*10m*10m CSGBox outside the room, which is a closed space with a single mesh. ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6dfdb7a7-a15b-4434-a304-cbb27848bae0) Result: There is still light leakage in the Editor, but the light leakage disappears when running the game, and the lighting is correct. ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/edad7432-c8db-41c4-bb2b-1e52c0e8b8f5) PS: Alternatively, if I add a CSGBox and then reopen the scene, the light leakage will also disappear.So it might be an issue with the editor update. ## Test 3 - How thick does the BOX need to be to completely block the light of DirectLight3D Tests have shown that the wall is at least 3 meters thick, and only a box with a single Mesh can completely block it. ## Testing of Other Light Sources I have tested SpotLight3D and OmniLight3D, and these two light sources do not have the above problem. Neither of them can illuminate the interior of a closed space, regardless of whether the closed space is a fully enclosed single Mesh or a combination of multiple Meshes. ## Bug Summary 1. There seems to be an issue with the indirect light calculation of DirectionLight3D when SDFGI is enabled. The indirect light from DirectionLight3D leaks into indoor scenes just like ambient light. **It's as if, as long as two surfaces are not part of the same mesh, even if they intersect, the intersecting edges are considered penetrable, resulting in light leakage. Only within a closed box made of a single mesh can the indirect light from DirectionLight3D be considered completely blocked.** 2. This light leakage issue also affects volumetric fog, causing a layer of fog to appear on thick walls when the volumetric fog energy is turned up. 3. REDDIT users have also discussed this issue https://www.reddit.com/r/godot/comments/1hincyz/light_leaks/ 4. This issue was reported by someone in 2021. #50770 After my testing and troubleshooting, it can be confirmed that the DirectLight3D light source has this issue when SDFGI is enabled, while SpotLight3D and OmniLight3D are normal with no light leakage. This is not a problem with parameter settings; it is a logical abnormality of DirectLight3D under SDFGI. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) My test project is 500MB, so I can't upload it. I can only provide a OneDrive download link. https://1drv.ms/u/c/fe3469be59fb19bd/IQAZDA_uiqF1SLHo0nz76RHTAWgioUXWKKVvpZtu_qyT-Qs?e=fa4scn
